prompt: HTML ol type attribute zero negative number rendering
answer:
The `
    ` `type` attribute controls the marker style, not the starting number. Its valid values are: - `1` — decimal numbers - `a` / `A` — lowercase/uppercase letters - `i` / `I` — lowercase/uppercase Roman numerals Use `start` to specify the first ordinal value: ```html
    1. First
    2. Second
    ``` HTML permits zero and negative `start` values, but browser support has historically been inconsistent. The search results specifically report that some browsers ignore them; older Opera versions honored `0` but could remove all markers for negative values. ([Blooberry](http://www.blooberry.com/indexdot/html/tagpages/o/ol.htm), [W3C HTML reference](https://w3c.github.io/html-reference/ol.html))
